reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of the abstaining deep classifier (DAC) is to extend a standard k-class neural network with an additional abstention output p_{k+1}, which allows the model to express uncertainty during training rather than simply assigning a hard label. This formulation enables the model to avoid making predictions on samples it deems unreliable, thereby mitigating the impact of label noise. The loss function is modified to normalize the abstention mass out of the real-class probabilities, ensuring that the model still learns from correct classifications while avoiding mislabeled examples. The auto-tuning of the abstention threshold α ensures that the model dynamically adjusts its willingness to abstain based on validation performance, preventing over-abstention or under-abstention. Lemmas 1 and 2 provide theoretical grounding: Lemma 1 shows that learning on true classes continues even when abstaining, preserving information flow; Lemma 2 warns that fixed α leads to extreme abstention rates over time, necessitating dynamic tuning. The data cleaning protocol leverages this trained DAC to identify and remove noisy samples by observing persistent errors on non-abstained validation data. In GSE context, this translates to identifying anomalous games where derived labels like 'beat-closing-line' are likely corrupted due to external factors such as weather or injury, allowing for more robust model training.
